newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares hit year high but end 1996 down.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares hit year high but end 1996 down.

text.p: Austrian shares hit a new year high of 1,155.15 points but the rally petered out due to lack of interest in the market, ending the year softer and traders predicted a weak start for 1997.
"I think we should be content with a close above 1,140 points," said one trader. The index would probably have closed firmer had there been more interest in the market, he noted.
Traders were more sceptical about the outlook for 1997 for the bourse.
"We will have to look reality in the eye again," said one. "There will be a lot of uncertainty in terms of currency and interest rates in 1997," he added.
The ATX index edged down 2.66 points or 0.23 percent to 1,140.19. Seven ATX shares rose, 11 fell and three remained unchanged.
Bank Austria was the leading gainer, climbing 4.22 percent to 420 schillings.

Creditanstalt preferred shares climbed 3.1 schillings to 500. Finance minister Viktor Klima on Friday reopened the tender for the sale of flagship bank Creditanstalt to allow current bidders a last chance to improve their offers.

Conservative Party chairman Andreas Kohl on Monday demanded an emergency session of parliament to push through changes to the law on privatisation and floatation in a last ditch attempt to prevent the bank being sold to Bank Austria.
The leading decliner of the session was fireproof material maker Radex Heraklith, shedding 2.83 percent to 343 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index lost 1.17 points or 0.27 percent to 429.20.
The January ATX future fell 1.8 points to 1,148. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
